chunks: Saad narrated from Musa ibn Umar from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'When you arrive at a town and intend to stay for ten days, complete the prayer (of four rak'at). If a ignorant person leaves it (praying full), there is no need for him to repeat it.'

key_terms.بَلْدَةً: a town or city, a settled place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayers when staying in one place for ten days?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the threshold for ending the state of travel (*safar*) by establishing a ten-day period of residence as the criterion for praying full (*tamam*) prayers. It highlights the Shia principle of *jahil* (ignorance) as a valid excuse for error, ensuring that those who mistakenly prayed short prayers due to lack of knowledge are not penalized with repetition, reflecting the juristic emphasis on ease and fairness in ritual obligations.
